claim.quote: Evidence for Neutrino Oscillations from the Observation of Electron Anti-neutrinos in a Muon Anti-Neutrino Beam

date.note: Published as Phys. Rev. D 64, 112007 (2001); submitted to arXiv 2001-04-27.

key_value_text.note: The paper does not itself state a single sigma significance figure in the text fetched; only the event excess and its statistical/systematic uncertainties.
key_value_text.quote: A total excess of 87.9±22.4±6.0 events consistent with electron anti-neutrino plus proton scattering to positron plus neutron was observed above the expected background. This excess corresponds to an oscillation probability of (0.264±0.067±0.045)%.

name: Evidence for Neutrino Oscillations from the Observation of Electron Anti-neutrinos in a Muon Anti-Neutrino Beam
notes: The brief specifically calls for LSND's antineutrino-appearance result to use the paper's own word 'evidence', never 'discovery'; this record uses result_type 'evidence' and the exact PRD 64, 112007 (2001) title, which contains 'Evidence' verbatim, satisfying A16's mechanical check.

significance.note: No single sigma significance figure is stated verbatim in the fetched text; the event excess (87.9 events) divided by its statistical uncertainty (22.4) is approximately 3.9, but this ratio is not itself quoted by the paper, so it is not asserted here as a stated significance.

summary.plain: LSND's final and strongest report that it saw more electron-antineutrinos than expected from a beam of muon-antineutrinos, at a distance too short to fit the standard three-flavour picture of how neutrinos change type. The collaboration called this evidence, not a discovery or observation.
summary.technical: Final LSND analysis of nu_mu_bar -> nu_e_bar appearance from mu+ decay at rest: excess of 87.9 +/- 22.4 (stat) +/- 6.0 (syst) beam-related nu_e_bar-candidate events, corresponding to an oscillation probability of (0.264 +/- 0.067 +/- 0.045)%, consistent with oscillations at Delta-m^2 in the 0.2-10 eV^2/c^4 range -- in tension with standard three-flavour oscillation and a principal motivation for subsequent short-baseline and sterile-neutrino experiments (KARMEN, MiniBooNE, MicroBooNE, SBN).

title: Evidence for Neutrino Oscillations from the Observation of Electron Anti-neutrinos in a Muon Anti-Neutrino Beam
why_it_matters: The LSND anomaly is one of the longest-standing puzzles in neutrino physics: if confirmed, it would require physics beyond three-flavour oscillation (e.g. one or more sterile neutrinos), and it directly motivated KARMEN, MiniBooNE, MicroBooNE and the Short-Baseline Neutrino programme at Fermilab.
